subject: Clarify data lifecycle SLAs and selective purging for MedTrust pilot
messages:
From: Bethany Lane <bethany.lane@medtrust.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Nunez <carlos@medtrust.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope — deletion SLA and selective purge questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we finalize scope for the MedTrust pilot we need to validate a few data lifecycle items from a compliance perspective so our legal/privacy team signs off. High level asks below — we attached a one-page list from legal for clarity (medtrust_evidence_request.xlsx).

1) Deletion SLA: For on-demand deletion requests from an admin or API call, what is the expected time-to-complete? We need an auditable timestamp and confirmation artifact.
2) Selective purge: Can we delete only certain fields (e.g., SSN, insurance numbers) while retaining transaction-level metadata for billing?
3) Embeddings & derived artifacts: If we delete a patient record, how do you handle embeddings derived from that text and any caches? Are embeddings treated as distinct objects that can be removed?
4) Evidence: What exportable evidence can you provide to show complete removal (logs, manifests, hash comparisons)?

Can you point us to a document/playbook or provide a short write-up on options and trade-offs? We’re trying to land on an approach that meets our 7-year records policy for clinical charts but also permits prompt-level redaction for ML-derived assets.

Appreciate a quick summary.

—Bethany
Bethany Lane
Lead Privacy Officer, MedTrust Health

Hi Bethany —

Thanks — great questions. I pulled together an overview and attached a short playbook (data_purge_playbook.pdf). High-level answers and config options below so we can decide which path aligns with your audit requirements.

1) Deletion SLA and artifact
- On-demand deletion via API or console: default workflow completes within 72 hours for tenant-level deletions (we can contract to 48 hours for Dedicated/private deployments).
- We emit a deletion manifest with timestamps and a signed hash summary (SHA-256) for the deleted objects; manifest plus system audit logs serve as the confirmation artifact.

2) Selective (field-level) purge
- Supported via our field-slice delete API: you can target named fields (e.g., ssn, insurance_id) and either remove values (nullify) or irreversibly redact (cryptographic shred).
- Trade-offs: nullify keeps schema and referential integrity for billing flows; irreversible redaction replaces content with a non-reversible token and removes ability to reconstruct the original.

3) Embeddings and derived artifacts
- Embeddings are treated as first-class objects linked to source IDs. You can: 1) delete embeddings by source ID (recommended), 2) run a purge that re-computes model-derived assets without the deleted inputs, or 3) mark embeddings as deprecated and exclude from search/indexing while retaining for billing analytics.
- Caches (KV caches, prefix caches) are invalidated as part of the deletion job; we run background compaction to remove orphaned cache entries within the same SLA window.

4) Evidence and verification
- Deliverables: deletion manifest (CSV), signed summary (SHA-256), audit log export (JSON/CSV), and an optional independent checksum report for exported archives.
- For Dedicated/private customers we can arrange an on-site or third-party verification run and provide a time-stamped certificate.

Next steps: Marissa — can you add technical notes on irreversible redaction and embedding purge approaches? Bethany/Carlos — if you can confirm whether you prefer field-null vs irreversible-redact for PHI, we’ll map to the pilot runbook.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot scope — deletion SLA and selective purge questions

Hi all —

Quick technical clarifications to supplement Ben’s summary. I’ll keep this focused and call out irreversible vs reversible behaviors and practical impact on derived assets.

- Field-null (reversible in that the record still exists): we set field to NULL/empty and retain the record. This preserves foreign keys and audit trails; works well if you need to keep transaction metadata for billing or analytics. No cryptographic proof of destruction for the field itself (because original content is not overwritten).

- Irreversible redaction (cryptographic shred): we overwrite the field with a one-way token derived via HMAC with customer-managed key (KMS option available). The original plaintext is gone; we store only the token. Audit evidence includes the HMAC seed ID and KMS rotation metadata.

- Embeddings: embeddings are indexed and optionally sharded by tenant+source-id. When you request deletion, our pipeline does the following in order: 1) mark source-id as deleted, 2) remove any pointers from search indexes, 3) queue embedding objects for deletion and execute compaction jobs that permanently remove vector blobs from storage. For embeddings cached in memory on serving nodes, we invalidate KV entries and push a TTL=0 update to serving nodes; ephemeral caches may take a few minutes to fully flush, but blob storage removal is permanent and covered by the SLA windows above.

- Snapshots & backups: we maintain regular snapshots for disaster recovery. Deletion jobs add an exclusion manifest so subsequent snapshot pruning removes deleted objects per retention rules. Important: if you require immediate removal from existing immutable snapshots, that requires a special escrow/rotation workflow and will be scoped as a one-time operational engagement.

- Evidence generation details:
  * Deletion manifest: list of object ids, types (record/embedding), timestamps, and signed hash
  * Audit export: API access logs, admin actions (who requested delete), and background job logs
  * Verification: we can provide a signed report and a sample re-hash run for selected object ids to show the pre/post hash mismatch.

Operational recommendation for MedTrust pilot:
- Use field-null for billing metadata retention where you need continuity.
- Use irreversible redaction for direct identifiers (SSN, MRN) to meet de-identification standards.
- Schedule an initial embedding purge pass for historical data at pilot cutover, then enable live delete-by-source-id for future deletes.

If you want, Priyom can sketch the exact API payloads and job id lifecycle so you can reference them in your evidence checklist.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
